# country-files

**The DX-cluster country file (cty.dat) — callsign prefix to entity, zone and coordinates**

- **Version recorded:** 20260906
- **Categories:** `contest`, `logging`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.country-files.com/>

## What it does

The lookup table every logger and contest program uses to turn a callsign into a DXCC entity, CQ and ITU zone, continent and coordinates: cty.dat and its siblings (cty.csv, swiftlog_cty.dat), as published by AD1C, installed under the shared data directory.

## Why you would want it

Loggers bundle a copy and it goes stale between their releases; new prefixes and entity changes arrive weekly. One current copy on the machine, updated like any other unit, is what AHRL's fan-out was trying to achieve by hand.

## Before it will work

Nothing. A program that reads it has to be pointed at /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/country-files/cty.dat, or names this unit in its own manifest's depends; none does yet.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install country-files --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- data (Jim Reisert AD1C's country files; free to use and redistribute with the copyright notice kept (copyright.txt in the release), https://www.country-files.com/): https://www.country-files.com/bigcty/download/2026/bigcty-20260906.zip (339,004 bytes)

## Known problems

The first data unit (D-049). No reader in the catalog consumes it from this path yet, so today it is a current cty.dat on disk and nothing more; the loggers still read their bundled copies until their manifests say otherwise. Installed as plain files, mode 0644, root-owned.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- A dated release most weeks, announced on country-files.com; each is a zip under /bigcty/download/<year>/bigcty-<date>.zip. Bump the URL, the hash, the size and `version` together.

## Where to get help with the software itself

The country-files.com site and its contact page; AD1C maintains the files and announces each release there.
